---
title: "Contributing"
---


Patches are welcome. A few things are worth knowing before you write code.

## The licence question comes first

The package is AGPL-3.0-or-later, and that is the whole story. There is no
contributor licence agreement to sign and no rights to assign: you contribute
under the AGPL, you keep your copyright, and the maintainer gets no rights over
your work that any other user does not also have.

If that is a problem for you, say so early, an unmergeable patch is a waste of
your time, not just ours.

**A new dependency is still a licensing decision.** ggplot2 and jsonlite are
MIT, *MASS* is GPL — all of them compatible with the AGPL, so nothing is
constrained today. What a dependency does bind is everyone downstream, so a
copyleft addition is a conversation before it is a pull request.

## What a good change looks like

* **A test that fails first.** Especially for a numerical fix: show the wrong
  number before you show the right one.
* **A note on the reasoning, not the change.** Comments that say what the code
  does are noise; comments that say what constraint made it necessary survive.
* **A table for every figure.** A new plot needs a companion that returns the
  numbers, and both belong in the Python twin as well.
* **`R CMD check --as-cran` clean.** No new notes, and no non-ASCII in `R/`.
* **roxygen2 with `@return` and `@examples`.** CRAN wants both, and the check
  in this repository confirms every exported function has them.

## What will be turned down

* Anything that writes to a Zotero library. Coding belongs in the plugin.
* A default that makes a coefficient look better, an automatic `uncoded`
  merge, a kappa that silently ignores multiply coded segments, an inertia
  share normalised to the dimensions kept.
* Statistics with no caveat attached. Where a number invites over-reading, the
  returned list has to carry whatever warns against it.
* A tidyverse dependency for something base R already handles.
* Reformatting mixed into a change of behaviour, which makes both unreviewable.

## If you change a coefficient

Start with [Testing](testing.qmd). Two frozen references have to be regenerated
together, in both packages, and the mutation check repeated afterwards. The
thing this project is built to prevent is precisely a coefficient that moves in
one language and stays put in the other two.

## Reporting a disagreement with the plugin

A number that differs from the plugin's means one of the two is wrong, and that
is worth an issue either way. Attach the export it happened on, or a coder
matrix small enough to reproduce it;
`qda_agreement()` output from both sides is usually enough to tell which side
is wrong.
